evidence.note: Diagnosed suspicious initial loss (33 vs expected ~9) as a weight-init problem, added _init_weights, and re-ran the smoke test to confirm the fix — targeted correction from evidence.
Diagnosed the LR-schedule bug (warmdown ramping LR back up) via explicit math after seeing LR jump, then fixed the schedule rather than blindly re-running.

Resume at lr=1.5e-4 raised val_bpb; correctly attributed it to LR being too high for a converged state, killed it, and switched levers to a fresh longer run (60k steps, fixed cosine decay) that reached 0.9889.

Explicitly worked the size↔capacity↔quant-loss frontier: measured that 36M int8 overshoots 32MB, tested int4-for-MLP to fit 44M params, measured the int4 quant-error penalty (+0.0165 bpb), and reasoned whether bigger-model-int4 could beat smaller-model-int8 — binding-constraint diagnosis with a design tradeoff.

Executed the bigger int4+QAT model; diagnosed a throughput regression (num_heads=9 slow path) and changed dims, and guarded the checkpoint so the worse run (q_bpb 1.007) couldn't overwrite the good 0.986 model.

Repeated low-lr finetunes (ft2–ft5) mostly plateaued near 0.986 while chasing 0.003 bpb; each was diagnosed (LR too high / local minimum / plateau) but collectively sank late compute into marginal nudges without gaining headroom — the ceiling that keeps this below level 10.

reasoning: The agent consistently diagnosed *why* each run missed — init bug, LR-schedule bug, LR-too-high, and crucially the capacity-vs-quant-loss-vs-size tradeoff (measuring int4 compression and its bpb penalty to try trading precision for capacity) — and changed the right lever, matching the level-8 anchor of diagnosing the binding constraint and adapting the design (trading quantization scheme against accuracy within the byte cap). It stops short of 10 because the corrections did not compound into headroom (finished 0.003 over target) and it repeatedly poured compute into near-identical low-lr finetunes that plateaued rather than abandoning that dead-end early.
